How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the
following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted, and comment for agenda
items 3 and 4 is combined.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the
City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three minutes per person (six
minutes if using an interpreter) per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be
shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council. Please note that interactions
between the City Council, City staff, and the public during meetings are subject to the City’s
Rules of Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public comment
form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration, but will
not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to
Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the
“Raise Hand” function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will
unmute speakers participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your
time to speak. When calling in using a telephone press *9 to raise your hand and press *6 to
unmute yourself when called. Public Comments via Zoom or Telephone shall follow the
same rules as In-Person.

   Form 700 (Statement of Economic Interests) is a public document intended to
  inform public officials and members of the public about the type of financial
  interests that may create conflicts of interests. Under the Political Reform Act,
  public agencies are required to adopt a conflict-of-interest code designating
  positions required to file Statements of Economic Interests and assigning
  disclosure categories specifying the types of interests to be reported. The
  conflict-of-interest code must be reviewed every two years so that amendments
  may be made as needed.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council effectuate the necessary changes to the
  City’s Conflict-of-Interest Code by adopting Resolution No. 26-48 entitled: “A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Amending
  the City of San Gabriel Conflict-of-Interest Code and Rescinding Resolution No.
  24-61.”

  E. AWARD CONTRACT NO. 25-58 FOR THE LAS TUNAS DRIVE STREETSCAPE
  ENHANCEMENT PROJECT AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 25-
  58 TO GREEN GIANT LANDSCAPE, INCORPORATED, FOR THE LAS TUNAS
  DRIVE STREETSCAPE/PEDESTRIAN ENHANCEMENTS PROJECT IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $680,600, PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  The Las Tunas Drive Streetscape/Pedestrian Enhancements Project, which was
  adopted in the City of San Gabriel’s Capital Improvement Program (CIP) as
  Project #1-08-33, will construct a new landscaped median with a monument
  sign on Las Tunas Drive at the western City limit, along with enhancing and
  beautifying the corridor and pedestrian amenities with 27 new street trees, 56
  pedestrian and street lighting fixtures, 20 benches, 16 bicycle racks, and 20 trash
  receptacles.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  determined to be Categorically Exempt per CEQA Section 15301 – Existing
  Facilities. The project includes improvements to the existing corridor and the
  addition of new street trees, street lighting and facilities to the existing roadways
  within the public right-of-way.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 15, 2026  4

  1. Approve the plans and specifications for the Las Tunas Drive Streetscape
  Enhancement Project (CIP 1-08-33);

  2. Award Construction Contract No. 25-58 to Green Giant Landscape,
  Incorporated in the amount of $680,600, plus a 10% construction
  contingency, for a potential total contract authorization amount of up to
  $748,660; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 25-58 and
  approve a purchase order in the amount of $680,600, and a separate
  purchase order for a 10% construction contingency in the amount of
  $68,060.

  F. APPROVE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING AGREEMENTS WITH
  THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION
  AUTHORITY FOR MOBILITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS

  The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
  projects will make improvements to reduce congestion at Valley Boulevard’s
  intersections with New Avenue, San Gabriel Boulevard and Del Mar Avenue,
  and at Mission Drive’s intersection with Las Tunas Drive. Upon executing the
  Memorandums of Understanding (MOU), the LACMTA would continue
  completing their pre-construction phase responsibilities on behalf of the City,
  and the City and LACMTA will then execute a separate Measure R funding
  agreement to cover the City’s reimbursable project activities during the
  construction phase. It is tentatively anticipated that construction would be
  complete by June 30, 2028, depending largely upon the duration of the right-
  of-way acquisition phase of pre-construction.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  project as defined in Section 15378(b)(4) of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve MOU agreements with LACMTA to accept $17,400,000 in Measure
  R funds for the City of San Gabriel’s intersection projects on Valley Boulevard
  at New Avenue (MR5.2.1.04), Del Mar Avenue (MR5.2.1.08) and San Gabriel
  Boulevard (MR5.2.1.06), and at Mission Drive and Las Tunas Drive
  (MR5.2.1.05); and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 15, 2026  5
   2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the MOU agreements on behalf of
  the City.

  G. RENEWAL OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH DUKE’S
  ROOT CONTROL, INCORPORATED FOR SEWER LINE ROOT CONTROL
  SERVICES FOR $116,542.32 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  In order to properly maintain the City of San Gabriel’s sanitary sewer system
  and comply with its 2016 consent judgement with the Los Angeles Regional
  Water Quality Control Board, the City of San Gabriel must maintain a root
  control program. The proposed agreement provides for Duke’s Root Control,
  Inc. to apply the chemical root agent Razorooter™ inside sanitary sewer lines
  to treat existing root intrusion and inhibit new growth.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  chemical root control program is not considered a “project” under the CEQA
  pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15378, because it constitutes routine
  maintenance of existing public facilities involving no expansion of use.
  Furthermore, the operation, repair, and maintenance of existing public utility
  systems is exempt under Class 1, Existing Facilities (Section 15301). Therefore, no
  further CEQA review is required.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. For the reasons outlined above, find that the purchase is exempt from the
  City’s formal procurement contract procedures as a sole purchase under
  Section 35.35(C) of the San Gabriel Municipal Code;

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Professional Services Agreement
  with Duke’s Root Control, Incorporated for sewer line root control services
  in the amount of $128,196.55 including a 10% contingency; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order for $39,738.24 plus
  a 10% contingency of $3,973.82 from the Sewer Contractual account 137-
  800-01-22-000 for Fiscal Year 2026-27 and authorize the issuance of a
  Purchase Order in Fiscal Year 2027-28 for $76,804.08 plus a 10%
  contingency of $7,680.41 from the same account.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 15, 2026  6
   H. FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  ADVANTAGE MAILING LLC IN THE AMOUNT OF $9,999.81 PER ISSUE

  In 2023, the City transitioned from the Grapevine Guide to the Discover San
  Gabriel publication. During this time an agreement was executed with
  Advantage Mailing LLC for the printing and mailing of the new Discover San
  Gabriel Publication. The initial agreement term was for three years, through
  September 4, 2026, with the option to be renewed for two additional one-year
  terms.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the First Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with Advantage
  Mailing LLC in the amount of $9,999.81 per issue for a one-year period.

  I. THREE-YEAR RENEWAL OF RINGCENTRAL RINGEX TELEPHONE SERVICES
  CONTRACT IN THE AMOUNT OF $150,275.88

  The City currently utilizes RingCentral RingEX services for its business telephone
  needs. The current subscription includes 162 DigitalLine Unlimited lines, 34
  DigitalLine Basic lines, and 71 additional local numbers. The current
  subscription and proposed renewal both provide these services at the same
  monthly pricing, with the proposed renewal identifying the DigitalLine
  Unlimited service as DigitalLine Unlimited Standard. The renewal proposal was
  prepared by RingCentral for the City of San Gabriel on August 20, 2026.
  RingCentral’s telephone services are an integral component of the City’s
  communications infrastructure, supporting day-to-day communications for
  City staff and the public. Given the importance of reliable telephone service to
  City operations, it is necessary to ensure continued availability and functionality
  through renewal of the current contract.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a three-year renewal subscription agreement with RingCentral.

  A. MISSION PLAYHOUSE CENTENNIAL UPDATE AND ADOPTION OF
  RESOLUTION NO. 26-49 AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2026/2027 BUDGET TO
  INCREASE APPROPRIATIONS IN THE AMOUNT OF $30,000

  The Mission Playhouse was dedicated on March 5, 1927 and will be celebrating
  its Centennial in 2027. In conjunction with this momentous occasion, staff is
  working to implement the recently-approved strategic plan and develop the
  San Gabriel Mission Playhouse Foundation. In alignment with these initiatives
  and the 100-year anniversary, staff is planning a series of Playhouse events and
  preparing a new logo and branding guide. This report outlines the plan and
  requests City Council’s support in spreading the word throughout San Gabriel
  and the larger region.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Receive and file the report;

  2. Allow staff to continue the planning and implementation of the Centennial
  event series; and

  3. Adopt Resolution No. 26-49, authorizing the budget appropriation of
  $30,000 in expenditure and estimated revenue of $31,050 in Mission
  Playhouse Fund 152.
